text: Arrets establishing and regulating the rights of notaries in surveying a noble's terrier
a censitaire on the terrier of the king, also owes the cens to a Seigneur pariager.
That a terrier signed by a Notary is legitimate even if not signed by Seigneur.
A censitaire may request the Seigneur re-do the terrier if he suspects Notary of making mistake.
Seigneur is allowed to choose the Notary to make the terrier.
Regulation describing the official procedure for requesting information from the censitaire for the terrier.
Restricting the ability of Seigneur to replace the notary creating the terrier.
A gardien of a lord in his minority may not revoke a judge's position
Requires Seigneurs to name Officers of Justice
Law allowing for the assignment of judges by Lord every three years within pareage.
A Judge's office may be sold but not divided by the Seigneur
Edict declaring judiciary offices revocable, even if purchased, for just compensation.
Intendents not allowed to revoke an officer of justice asigned by local lord unless they have permission from King.
Seigneur not allowed to create a Lieutenant without permission from King.
Forbids tenants of the Lord to be judges.
Forbids Seigneurial judges from being Judges of waters and forests.
Establishing the competence of Local Judges to hear cases involving Seigneurial Agents
In pecuniary matters (matiere reelle) the Sieigneur can be brought to trial in his own court.
Disallows Seigneurial judges from judging crimes in commited in community woods.
Seigneurs required to indemnify merchants robbed on roads they tax.
All tolls on Loire and its tributaries eliminated.
Abolished all internal tolls not legitimate.  Those that exist must maintain roads etc….  And that they only tax what they're allowed.
All peages on Seine and its tributaries (up to Rouen) abolished.  Reimbursed owners of eliminated tolls.  Created new Aides taxes to pay for this.
Forbids collecting a toll without Royal permission.
Eliminates illegitimate peages under pain of confiscation of "corps et de fief".  Required all existing tolls to be officially registered.
Arret stating that tolls in existence for at least 40 years are legitimate.
Cour des Grands Jours orders registration and/or suppression of peages in Auvergne, Bourbonnois, La Marche, Combraille, Lyonnois, Forez, Beaujolois, Maconnois.
All owners of peages, bacs, bateux, ponts, and other rights must prove they had legitimate right for at least 100 years.
Ordonnance on Gabelles prohibits any local taxes on salt.
Edicts requiring written confirmation of request in Edict of 1668.
All peages on Loire and Cher rivers suppressed unless royal titles presented to Intendant within 3 months under penalty of 3,000 livre fine.
Commission on peages suppresses "1,200" throughout kingdom under orders of Louis XV. (p 315, Renauldon).
Orders that peages must be renewed with each change in crown.
That a peage payable in goods is also payable in silver.
That a corveable is not obligated to rent working stock (betail) to fulfill his duties.
That in certain circumstances the Seigneur must house and feed the corveable.
Limiting the number of beasts required from the corveable to two oxen.
That the corveable can convert labor due into cash payment.
Restricting the cases in which children are subject to the corvee.
Prohibiting Seigneur from requiring corvee without "precise title"
Regulating the conditions of corvee.
Sets the times that a subject can obligated to perform corvee.
Regulates the number and nature of corvees.
Requiring silver payment for missed corvee.
Prohibitions on the maltreatment of corveables.
Corvees in good title are imprescriptible.
That is the corveable is in one noble's jurisdiction but his ox in another, he still needs to bring the ox.
Regulating the appropriate titles necessary to invoke the corvee.
That notaries are exempt from the corvee.
Ordonnace of Charles the Bald that all measures of greater than the royal measures be reduced.
Francis I orders the unit of length "l'aulne de roi" be used throughout kingdom.
Ordonnances requiring weights & measures be brought in line to those of Paris.
Publication of Savery's "Parfait Negociant" at the request of Colbert.
Arret prohibiting charging for the use of measures established by Seigneur.
Ordonnance on standardization of weights & measures.
